clue.text: Upstart cut short rendezvous after knock-back

indicators.note: 'after' places the shortened meeting place behind the turned-round knock
the 'back' of 'knock-back' tells us to read the word for knock in reverse

parts.note: to knock is to rap

indicators.note: something cut short loses its final letter, so the meeting place is docked at the end

parts.note: a rendezvous is a meeting place, a venue

explanation.surface: A jumped-up person cuts a meeting short after being rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock-back' looks like one word meaning a rejection, but it splits: 'back' turns the word for knock round, and 'cut short' docks the meeting place's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a social climber who has newly risen to wealth or status, which is what an upstart is.

clue.text: River, one agriculturalist brought up with conservationists, getting dirtier

definitions.note: a noun here: something that makes things dirty

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a means one
Jethro Tull was an English agricultural pioneer who invented the seed drill
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Something fouling the river is blamed on a farmer and the green lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: A TULL 'brought up' gives LLUTA. 'getting' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollutant is a substance that contaminates and fouls things, a polluting agent.

clue.text: Mastermind rescheduled, test cricket is on

indicators.note: rescheduled means rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A clever plan: the test match has been moved and play is going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mastermind' looks like a verb or the TV quiz, but it is a noun for a genius.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket scientist is the stock example of a brilliant person, a genius.

clue.text: Lead sinks in ship designs

indicators.note: the leading letter drops down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: to ship goods is to send them

explanation.surface: Heavy weights go down in a shipbuilder's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the metal, but it is the first letter: in SEND the S sinks to the end. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are aims or purposes, as designs are intentions.

clue.text: Free meal, excluding starter, overwhelming success

indicators.note: overwhelming means surrounding and engulfing something
the starter is the first letter, here removed

parts.note: lunch is a meal
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A free lunch, minus the first course, is a huge triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free meal' tempts as a free lunch phrase, but 'Free' alone is the definition; dropping the starter leaves UNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten or release, which is what to free means.

clue.text: Author's career to come to an end

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: to career is to rush along headlong
to come to an end is to die

explanation.surface: A writer's working life is about to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is a verb here, to hurtle along, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is a famous novelist, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Prince wearing tie once more to succeed

indicators.note: a thing wearing something has it on its body, so it goes inside

parts.note: to relace is to tie laces again

explanation.surface: A royal dresses in a tie again to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace someone is to take over from them, to follow on in their role.

clue.text: Extravagant Kate Moss gets designer chimney

indicators.note: extravagant means wildly over the top, so the letters run wild

parts.note: CK is Calvin Klein, the fashion designer label

explanation.surface: The supermodel goes wild and acquires a designer label.
explanation.walkthrough: KATE MOSS rearranged gives SMOKESTA; CK completes it. 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smokestack is a tall industrial flue, a kind of chimney.

clue.text: Routine job to bore teacher

parts.note: to bore a hole is to drill
an instructor is a teacher

explanation.surface: A dull job that bores the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Routine job' is a playful definition: drill (military routines) is this person's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill instructor trains recruits in parade-ground routines, a job built on repetition.

clue.text: Go into medical field seen on US hospital drama

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece seen on another sits above it

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
ER is the American TV series set in an emergency room

explanation.surface: A specialism is featured on a US medical TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come or go into a place.

clue.text: With it, detectives follow clue extremists left behind

indicators.note: 'follow' puts the detectives after the trimmed clue
the extreme letters of the word clue are left behind, keeping only its inner pair

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives pursue a clue once the extremists have fled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with it is mentally clear and alert, which is what lucid means.

clue.text: Sit up after python goes to pot for charmer

indicators.note: 'after' puts the jumbled sit behind the jumbled python
going to pot means falling into ruin, so the letters of python are thrown into disorder
'up' in the sense of things being amiss, so the three letters of sit are stirred

explanation.surface: A snake charmer's python sits up and wrecks the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to pot' jumbles python and 'up' stirs sit separately; 'charmer' suggests a snake charmer, fitting the python of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotist puts people under a spell, so is a kind of enchanter or charmer.

clue.text: Posh bird in cinema's items to play with

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class, posh usage
Kes is a 1969 British film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: An upper-class woman at the pictures has toys to amuse herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' suggests a girlfriend in British slang, but here it is the kestrel of the film Kes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukes are ukuleles, small guitars that are instruments to be played.

clue.text: Jet-setter's relatives regularly squeezed by bank clerk

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: being squeezed by something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk who serves customers

indicators.note: taking letters at a regular interval from relatives, here every third one starting with the first

explanation.surface: A globetrotter's family members are routinely crushed by a bank employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' here takes every third letter, starting from the first, giving RAV; it lands just after the teller's opening T.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-setter is someone who flies around the world a great deal, a frequent traveller.

clue.text: Rank criminal after bishop's neighbour

indicators.note: the criminal comes after the bishop's neighbour

parts.note: on a chessboard the knight starts next to the bishop
a hood is a gangster, a criminal

explanation.surface: An utter crook lives next door to the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul, but it is the definition, a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A knighthood is an honour conferring a title, a rank in the honours system.

clue.text: Wrong to get into bath spilling alcoholic drink

indicators.note: one piece gets into another, so sin goes inside
spilling throws the letters of bath out of place

parts.note: a wrong is a sin

explanation.surface: It is wrong to climb into the tub while knocking over a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' jumbles the tub's letters into ABTH, and 'to get into' puts the wrong inside. Absinth is also spelt absinthe.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, a potent liquor.

clue.text: Harmony from trio of entertainers seen two to three times

indicators.note: the three-letter run is seen twice over
a trio is three, so the first three letters of entertainers are taken
the count runs on from two towards three times, adding one more letter of the run

explanation.surface: Agreement comes from a group of three performers who appear two or three times.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT (the first three letters of 'entertainers') appears 'two to three times': twice in full and then a third of the way again, giving ENT ENT E.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, a state of concord.

clue.text: Short-lived ecstasy on her ample bust

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of her ample are smashed up

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled thrill on her generous chest does not last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as a chest but signals breaking up the letters. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral describes something fleeting, lasting only a brief time.

clue.text: Revolutionary widget with German investment caught on

indicators.note: an investment is something put inside, so the German letter goes within
something revolutionary turns things upside down, so the letters of widget are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radical new gadget with German money behind it has taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: WIDGET rearranged gives TWIGED, and 'investment' puts G inside to make TWIGGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for understanding something, so twigged means grasped or realised.

clue.text: First of injections in bum is brief

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a dosser is a down-and-out, a bum

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter

explanation.surface: The first jab in the backside does not take long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' reads as a backside but means a vagrant, DOSSER in British slang. 'brief' is a noun, a lawyer's file.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of papers on a case, as a lawyer's brief is.

clue.text: Unplanned victims of netting, how might cricketers get out?

explanation.surface: Fish caught by accident, and the ways a cricketer can be dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter can be out 'caught', so a fielder may get a batter out by a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing jargon for unwanted sea creatures caught in nets; also, read as two words, the means by which a fielder dismisses a batter.

clue.text: Nasty shock having died in guillotine

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to guillotine someone is to behead them
d is short for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dreadful jolt for someone who died under the blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a fright, but it means a mass of hair. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedhead is untidy hair after sleep, so a messy unkempt shock of hair.

clue.text: Sterile and extremely dire protest when overturned

indicators.note: overturned means the whole run is turned round
the extremes of dire are its first and last letters

parts.note: a sit-in is a form of protest
as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'

explanation.surface: Clean, but a protest when things are very bad gets overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when overturned' turns round the whole run DESITINAS; 'and' is a link after the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sanitised has been cleaned of germs, so it is sterile.

clue.text: Heartlessly hunt in total silence

definitions.note: a noun here, while the answer is the adjective for keeping quiet

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sum is a total

indicators.note: heartlessly means losing the heart, leaving only first and last letters

explanation.surface: Searching without compassion in complete quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'hunt' give HT, which goes into SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtum is Yiddish-derived slang for keeping quiet, as in 'keep shtum'.

clue.text: Island base for choppers invaded by America

indicators.note: invaded by means having something enter it

parts.note: the gum is the base in which teeth, choppers, are set

explanation.surface: An island helicopter base is overrun by the Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppers' suggests helicopters, but here it is slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific, a small island.

clue.text: Persuade crew member to accept amateur

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in

parts.note: the cox steers a rowing crew

explanation.surface: Talk a rower round into taking on a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing the cox steers the boat and is part of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade gently by flattery or urging.

clue.text: Tyrannosaurus Rex in lea openly starts to eat prehistoric creature

indicators.note: 'to' simply attaches the next piece on
the starts of the five words are their first letters

parts.note: to bite is to eat

explanation.surface: A T. rex in a meadow openly begins to devour an ancient animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letters of Tyrannosaurus, Rex, in, lea, openly: TRILO. A lea is a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilobite is an extinct marine arthropod known from fossils, an ancient animal.

clue.text: External network device failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means losing the first letter

parts.note: a router is a device that directs traffic on a computer network

explanation.surface: An outside box that connects to the internet will not boot up.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer means on the outside, which is what external means.

clue.text: Spaniard that fights Frenchman's a little yellow

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
a tad is a little
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A Spanish fighter thinks a Frenchman is somewhat cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' suggests cowardice, but OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull, a Spanish fighter in the ring.

clue.text: Right Reverend, extra large trousered

indicators.note: trousered means pocketed, taken in, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: A Right Reverend clergyman wears outsize trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Reverend' reads as a bishop's title, but 'Right' is the definition, and the answer sits inside 'reveREND EXTRA Large'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextral means right-handed or on the right-hand side.
